copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. Iraq v Norway in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Tuesday, and the model and the market disagree on the Iraq side by +11.8pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

Public Elo rates Norway 220 points higher than the other side (Iraq 1540, Norway 1760). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Iraq to win at 18%, the draw at 17%, and Norway to win at 65%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. Iraq on the win side reads 18%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Iraq to win at 6%, the draw at 15%, and Norway to win at 78%. On the Iraq side specifically the market reads 6%, which prices out at American odds of +1438. Compared against the model's 18%, that's the +11.8pp gap the Pick rests on.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Iraq the lower bound is 14%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +7.4pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff 26 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Iraq a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +11.8pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: The market reads Iraq as a 6% chance; our Elo prior reads them at 18%. A +11.8pp gap on a longshot side is where the engine finds its biggest Picks.
copy.title: Iraq v Norway · the model leans Iraq
